To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pooled‐sample design used in NHANES is an efficient method to estimate population distributions and that the estimates based on the pooled‐sample method are comparable to those based on the individual‐sample method.

the pooled‐sample approach can be successfully used to reduce the number of analyses in biomonitoring studies, and the pooled‐sample design implemented in NHANES is effective for estimating percentiles of PCB153 concentrations in specific subpopu­lations of the US.
the weighted pooled‐sample approach is feasible and that the estimates based on pooled‐sample data are similar to those based on individual‐sample data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to estimate the concentration distribution of environmental compounds in the US based on a pooled‐sample biomonitoring design.
the development and application of a statistical methodology to estimate the distributions of concentrations (or concentrations of metabolites) of chemicals in the US population.
the use of a weighted pooled‐design to estimate the distributions of environmental compounds or metabolites in the general US population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper describes the use of a weighted pooled‐design in NHANES for the analysis of PCBs.
the use of a pooled‐sample biomonitoring design is feasible and can be used in the future to reduce the cost of biomonitoring for polychlorinated compounds in the population.

there is no evidence of any significant risk to the health of the public as a result of exposure to the levels of PCBs in the environment, but there is some evidence that there is no significant risk to the population from the exposure to the levels in the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel method for estimating percentiles of concentrations of environmental chemicals in the population based on the use of pooled samples.
the weighted pooled‐sample method is an efficient way to estimate the distribution of environmental compounds in the population, and it can be used to reduce the cost of biomonitoring.
the pooled sample design is a viable alternative to the individual sample design for estimating the concentrations of environmental compounds in subpopulations of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pooled‐sample design used in NHANES can reduce the cost and time required to analyze environmental chemicals in body fluids.
pooled samples can be used to reduce the costs of environmental monitoring.
pooled‐sample designs are a cost‐effective alternative for estimating population distributions of environmental compounds in the US, and they can also reduce the burden on study participants.
